Will publish the spec now (assuming all deposits are valid) https://github.com/goerli/altona ``` [2020-06-24 20:54:23] INFO powchain: Processing deposits from Ethereum 1 chain deposits=512 genesisValidators=241 ``` I think we have to wait longer nearly half the deposits are invalid wow that's a lot so, altona is already a full success 🥳 Oops, do the invalid deposits having invalid Merkle proofs? This could be us I'll try and check all deposits now from what i could see these were all with bad signatures Got 386 bad deposits. Here's a full debug dump of the processing, incl tx details, bad deposits list and current registry contents: https://gist.github.com/protolambda/e47c1adc0bd8c4d42e438d1815587d35 <@!557201004060213248> I am going to guess all those with invalid depoists have a genesis fork version of ``` 0x00000000 ``` I'll try that version and see if they are valid with that Hmm, nope, still 386 bad deposits hmm just spit-balling If that is _the_ problem with deposits, we could just make a **constant** (rather than a **config var**) called `DEPOSIT_FORK_VERSION` that is not configurable across different chains ah I'll try witti fork version hmm genesis_val_root and current_fork still give sig domain isolation across chains for any important (slashable) messages in that case they may have been using the old bls spec possible although 386 deposits failing with that is odd, I would assume everyone is updated to the latest BLS spec wait, it's 386 still, but different ones Wow that's strange.. even more bizarre lol implies some set are due to fork and some set are broken with both forks raise your hand if you own pubkeys in the original failed list Here are the different bad-deposit lists: https://gist.github.com/protolambda/54d0090b73be8c94b5a97cda77c74347 I'll make a version with only the valid ones per fork version now. Oh no, there are also common bad deposits between the two So there's at least 3 different signature methods there has to be given 386*2 is greater than the amount of deposits 🙂 so there are altona fork versions, 0x00 fork versions, and ones bad on both I'm finding our deposits in the invalid set. We currently have compile-time flags for specifying the BLS version, so I'll double what ended up being used. jacek shared a pubkey of nimbus and it looks like one of the many bad deposits > raise your hand if you own pubkeys in the original failed list 🙋‍♂️ The prysm deposits are bad. Will have to resend them. We used the onyx config for sending them deposits. Internally we'll improve how we load these configs We are supposed to target the new 12.x spec, right? yes And custom fork version, see config of afri We should be using this value `GENESIS_FORK_VERSION: 0x00000121` Yeah I just saw the config. I was under the impression it's the same config as mainnet Deposits 0 through 127 are the Teku ones I believe - looking OK if I'm reading things right. running a script now to run through all deposits with each version, and bucket them by version. By version: https://gist.github.com/protolambda/17aa67b1aae7feaa009bbcd62590c4dc deposit #450 is one of mine and has a correct version. And the first 128 are correct too, so Teku is correct as well The pubkey of Jacek is listed under unknown version TLDR: 256 with 0 version (likely Prysm, same as Onyx. Maybe lighthouse too?), 256 with altona version (Teku + EF), 130 with unknown version (Nimbus + 2 extra?) Prysm are the ones with 0 version but only 128. I'll resend the deposits with correct version in an hour Lighthouse deposits are from address `0x8fa35b1ff7320b7b1dc24ef1bc711f699dd0623b` let me check yes that are lighthouse deposits starting at 128 cc <@!361447803194441738> Goerli has not implemented the Berlin EIPs yet, correct? if the BLS precompiles were in place we could add the deposit contract proxy to catch some of the invalid signature stuff higher upstream I think I've found the problem with our deposits and I've just made a single test one here: https://goerli.etherscan.io/tx/0xc7c4cc014d9cebd46c8dfdfe1d69e48a21e59392a70354d38fc848291187232e Can someone please verify whether it's accepted? <@!553610810652622860> signature seems valid, checked with a script here (change details to match your tx if you use it): https://github.com/protolambda/eth2-val-tools/blob/master/check_deposit.py yes, I used your script to find the problem I highly recommend you make a signature check through some extra tool part of the process of making deposits, to avoid problems in the future Yep, looks like ours were invalid too. Not sure how, perhaps I just didn't save the config file before I used it or something. Oh, I forgot to pass the `--testnet-dir` flag 🤦‍♂️ Ha 🙂 I have re-sent the 128 for Prysm. The last 128 deposits (sender: 0xa70c) were from us And checked them <@!363800010518822915> ? <@!203220829473996800> yep 👍 <@203220829473996800> how do you run this? https://github.com/protolambda/eth2-val-tools/blob/master/build_deposits.sh sorry, this: https://github.com/protolambda/eth2-val-tools/blob/master/check_deposit.py oh right `eth2spec` is on pip now It's on pip. Just create a venv (`python -m venv venv`), go into it (`. venv/bin/activate`), install latest spec (`pip install eth2spec`), and run while still in the venv (`python check_deposit.py`). (I know you know python, just documenting steps for anyone else who wants to give this a try) Alrighty, my deposits are in from address `0x8fa35b1fF7320B7B1DC24ef1Bc711F699Dd0623b`. I checked one of them with Proto's tool and it was good. `GOOD`, even.. not just lowercase good. I only had the "BAD" case first, and decided to print "GOOD" for good measure. And never refactored the if arms. Debug scripting be like that. But at least it's quick to script anything with spec 🙂 The caps works for me. Nothing like a good, firm response! > I highly recommend you make a signature check through some extra tool part of the process of making deposits, to avoid problems in the future <@!203220829473996800> We do a check to ensure that the amount supplied is consistent with the deposit root, but we don't check the signature at deposit time. We could pretty easily do this, considering we store the voting keypair alongside the deposit data file. Still not protected against user error of failing to supply flags though. I guess that will be less of a problem when we're not running use disparate specs. <@!550420431744794624> and <@!415109946682769408> and others have been working on python deposit tooling, which can function as a more mainnet-grade deposit check you could integrate. For now the import spec + that short script will work though So did we hit min genesis deposits? 42% have reached the follow distance from my view. But there's a bunch still too close to head I think. So likley genesis will be in the middle of night for afri again 😂 Matters less this time with the distribution of vals across all the client teams I have to admit, that makes me quite happy. 🙂 Sorry Afri.
